portfolio_narrative: This is a small, high-confidence estate of three guest-facing drug coverage tests, all fully regenerable with no unresolved bindings. Two of the three tests are the same scenario wearing different drug data — a generic-on-formulary case and a brand-non-formulary case walk identical steps and identical assertion shapes — so they collapse into one parameterized regeneration instead of two maintained implementations. The third test proves a distinct, unrelated capability (health plan context propagation) and is migrated unchanged. Net effect: one fewer implementation to maintain going forward with zero loss of asserted coverage.

decisions.rationale: This test and TIM-002 walk the identical guest-plan-search-detail flow against the identical page bindings, differing only in which drug is searched and what formulary status is expected. Keeping them as two hand-written implementations doubles maintenance cost for zero additional business coverage; folding them into one parameterized test proves both the on-formulary generic case and the non-formulary brand case from a single implementation.

decisions.rationale: Proves the non-formulary brand-drug counterpart of the same coverage-lookup scenario as TIM-001, using the same steps and page bindings with only the drug data and expected formulary status differing. This is a data variation of one intent, not a second distinct test, so it should be folded into the merged implementation as a second parameterized case.

decisions.rationale: This test proves a distinct, business-critical concern — that the plan a guest selects is the plan actually reflected during their coverage lookup — with no meaningful overlap to the drug-coverage tests. It is cheap to run, fully regenerable, and carries a genuine application-reading assertion, so it should be ported as-is.

merge_groups.rationale: Both tests execute the identical guest entry, plan/drug-list configuration, search-and-add, and detail-view steps against identical page bindings; the only variation is the drug searched (generic vs. brand) and the resulting formulary/tier text, including a mirrored test-data sanity check on the on/off drug-list flag. This is a single coverage-lookup intent parameterized over drug data, not two distinct tests, so the platform should regenerate one parameterized test with two cases.
